narrative.text: Morning briefing. The usual stack of reports, cables, and agenda items. Vyktor is moving through the intelligence digest at his usual pace — eight items in four minutes, each one dispatched with a sentence or two and a recommendation. Then he pauses. Not a long pause. But Vyktor Reznik does not pause during briefings. The pause itself is information.
Arcturian ambassador's office. Requesting a formal meeting. Sooner than protocol requires for a newly sworn-in government.
He reads directly from the cable — a rare concession. Vyktor usually summarizes. When he quotes directly, he wants you to hear the exact wording, not his interpretation of it.
Possibly routine. Cole is known for aggressive diplomatic positioning. Possibly not. The protocol window for an inaugural meeting is three weeks. This request came four days after you took office.

He places the cable on top of the stack. He does not flag it. He does not recommend a course of action. He simply places it where you will see it again, on top of everything else, impossible to miss. Vyktor's version of a raised eyebrow.

The Gazette piece. Now Cole requesting a meeting four days into my term. Either my government leaks like a sieve or Cole has the best intelligence operation in the hemisphere. The first is more likely. The second is more dangerous. Both are possible.
